subject: comet near the sun
title: What If a Comet Crashed Into the Sun? Thousands Have Tried

scenes.text: What if a comet slammed into the Sun? Thousands have tried. The Sun never noticed.
Since 1995 the SOHO spacecraft has spotted over 5,000 comets, most found by volunteers scanning its pictures online.
Most are Kreutz sungrazers: fragments of one giant comet that broke apart centuries ago, perhaps 20,000 pieces.
They dive to within about 50,000 kilometres of the Sun's surface, straight through its outer atmosphere.
No comet has ever been seen to reach the surface. The heat and the pull tear it apart first. Most simply evaporate.
So the crater never happens. A mountain of ice meets a star and vanishes like breath on a window. The Sun doesn't flicker.

description:
What if a comet hit the Sun? It happens constantly: since 1995 the ESA/NASA SOHO spacecraft has discovered more than 5,000 comets, the 5,000th in March 2024, most of them by volunteers scanning its images.
Most are Kreutz sungrazers, fragments of one giant comet that broke up centuries ago, which pass within about 50,000 km of the Sun's surface; none has ever been seen to reach the surface, because they evaporate in the solar atmosphere first.
What should we run through next?

first_comment: The 5,000th SOHO comet was spotted by a volunteer in the Czech Republic who has found over 200 himself. What should we throw at the Sun next?
